What becomes of a soul... When a person dies?

 Many rumors and mythos have spread accross the world. Many different rituals and rites have been used for centuries. No one knows for sure... But a rumor has spread. 

A rumor of a new ferryman.

Bo had lived his life as one grand adventure, one of new beginings. After a time in a city, where death had become fuzzy and muddled... where the souls of the dead had begun to rise again. Bo had made a descision. The dead need to rest. Their time has come, and the balance must be upheld.

 Upon one's death, a shadowy figure appears near the dying person. A slow and melodical lullaby played on a banjo herolds the coming of death, and eases the soul. It beckons the pain to evaporate away, and bring peace to the dying's mind. 

A flash of light in your final moment, the life you lived played out before you, is met with a curious looking ethereal pseudodragon giggling as it boops your nose. The now dead, finds themself ridng a few feet above the river styx, on a flying carpet. 

To whatever language you speak, or what ever form you take, there is one on the carpet with you. As a changling in life near the end, he appears as one of your own race, to help comfort you as he delivers you to the afterlife.

"Well howdy there fella!" He greets you with a warm smile.
"We got a ways ta go, how about you be tellin me your name, mine's Bo! And this here's Lucy" the pseudodragon waves from his shoulder.

If a person is near death, but there time has not yet come... The shadowy figure would still appear and play the lullaby, and your life would still flash before your eyes. But that person... would wake up in the land of the living still. The only image they would remember from their near death experience, Lucy booping their nose. A moment would pass before the living would soon forget the giggling pseudodragon, as she beamed across the sky leaving a rainbow in her wake.

This is the grandest adventure of Bo Harkness, now a true captain of his vessel. To comfort the dearly departed, making friends with all he transports. To listen to your life's story.
